summary: Feed s175_triple is degraded with 3 faults: 25.5% one-way TCP sessions, 6.8% genuine packet drops, and 11.0% frames truncated to 256B. All three break IDS requirements for bidirectional, full-payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: Traffic is not aggregated bidirectionally before the IDS. 37 of 145 TCP sessions (25.5%) show only one direction, indicating asymmetric routing with separate TAP/SPAN feeds not joined or a single-direction SPAN/mirror.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions to track TCP state, reassemble streams and detect exploits. One-way visibility causes missed handshakes, broken flow reassembly, and high false-negative rate for IDS signatures.

recommended_fix.why: IDS profile requires both directions. Aggregate client-to-server and server-to-client for same flow onto this single IDS feed at the packet broker to restore full session visibility.

findings.root_cause: Genuine packet loss in the visibility path, not caused by slicing (verified via IP header length). 124 of 1836 TCP packets (6.8%) show gaps/sequence holes, typical of SPAN/mirror oversubscription, buffer exhaustion, or broker egress drops. Tool overload is healthy, so loss is upstream of the IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS loses TCP segments, fails to reassemble payloads, misses attack signatures that span multiple packets, and generates incomplete flow logs. 6.8% loss far exceeds 1% threshold for reliable detection.

recommended_fix.why: Replace lossy SPAN/mirror with physical TAP and ensure packet broker has sufficient buffer/capacity. TAP provides lossless copy and eliminates SPAN drop behavior under load.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker slicing/snaplen configured to ~256 bytes. 213 of 1930 frames (11.0%) are cut short, most to 256 bytes, stripping L7 payload.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature matching and exploit detection. Truncated frames hide HTTP bodies, TLS handshakes, and attack payloads, causing IDS to miss application-layer threats.

recommended_fix.why: Disable slicing or increase snaplen to at least 1518 bytes (tool max_frame_bytes) for this IDS feed so full payload is delivered for inspection.
